$comment: Canonical vocabulary and field contract for a resource record in public/resources.json. Language-neutral JSON because three consumers must read it: the client (via shared/resource-schema.ts), the Vercel functions (same module), and the Python ingest scripts (via scripts/_schema.py). Do not hand-edit a vocabulary in one of those consumers — change it here.

fields.$comment_flags: Flag fields are written only when true and omitted otherwise — never written as false. diffFields() in src/lib/admin-changes.ts coerces an absent flag to false so toggling one off on a record that never carried it is not a change.

vocabularies.$comment_resource_type: audio and other carry no records today but are declared by the refresh-resources Researcher template, so they stay in-vocabulary rather than failing a legitimate curation run.
vocabularies.$comment_granularity: How much of a teacher's search a resource has already done, judged from the page the URL opens (not the publisher). activity: one thing students do in a single sitting (a simulation, game, video, interactive, worksheet, problem set, article). lesson: a teacher-facing plan for one lesson, with its materials. unit: a bounded set on ONE topic or overall expectation (a unit plan, a short series, a one-topic playlist or workbook) whose contents are visible on the page. collection: an index, hub, course, library or site front page spanning several topics, where the teacher still has to find the thing to use. tool: an open-ended tool or data source with no lesson content of its own (a graphing calculator, map viewer, data portal, writing platform). reference: background for the teacher rather than something to teach with (curriculum documents, encyclopedia articles, PD frameworks). When torn between two, choose the broader. Written by the enrichment routine from the fetched page and by the refresh routine's review stage; see intake for the gate on new records.
vocabularies.$comment_link_status: Union of the link-check ledger vocabulary (scripts/link-check.py) and the enrichment verdicts (scripts/enrich-resources.py). The dead/dead_domain vs error/blocked split is load-bearing: 'the site said so' must never collapse into 'our request failed' — a denied egress proxy once recorded 580 live URLs as blocked. Advisory only; nothing is auto-suppressed on a link verdict.

intake.$comment: The gate on new records, enforced by scripts/validate-resources.py in CI. Most of the catalog is hubs, courses and front pages tagged as if they taught one expectation, which hands a teacher a website to dig through instead of a resource. So every record added on or after granularity_required_from must carry an accepted granularity and a URL deeper than a site's front page. Older records are classified by the enrichment routine as it reaches them, and are not held to this.

admin.$comment: Allowlists for the Database Manager changeset. src/lib/admin-changes.ts and api/admin-push.ts both derive from here, replacing the two hand-synced copies that api/ could not share because it cannot import from src/. Curation-pipeline fields (grade_band, resource_type, access_type, province, jurisdiction, modality, accessibility, instructional_modes, and all provenance) stay out.
admin.$comment_vocab: Editable keys whose values must stay in-vocabulary. Without this, validateChanges() in api/admin-push.ts checked type and length only, so an admin edit could widen subject or strand to any string.

invariants.name: is_paid_matches_access_type
invariants.description: is_paid is fully derivable from access_type and agrees on all records today. Kept as a field because three readers use it directly (src/lib/use-filtered-resources.ts, src/components/resource-card.tsx), but enforced so the two cannot drift.

invariants.name: jurisdiction_matches_province
invariants.description: jurisdiction is the snake_case expansion of province; see vocabularies.jurisdiction_by_province.

invariants.name: unique_ids
invariants.description: Resource ids are the changeset key for the admin Database Manager, so a duplicate would make an edit ambiguous.

invariants.name: flags_never_false
invariants.description: Flag fields are omitted rather than written false; see fields.flags.
invariants.rule: for f in fields.flags: f absent or f === true
